The interaction between successive impulses introduces nonlinearity, enabling complex behaviors such as oscillation. Spontaneous emission acts as a background signal that can dominate behavior under static conditions, introducing variability. These primitives form a unified framework for understanding how organisms integrate environmental inputs into adaptive responses. Failure modes include saturation of impulse response and loss of oscillatory dynamics due to excessive interaction effects or lack of spontaneous activity.
